recent_posts.title: Non-technical virtual assistant ships full Laravel app in 5 days using Claude Code
recent_posts.summary: Kayla Helmick, a virtual assistant with no coding background, built a full-featured Laravel memorial website in 5.5 days using Laravel Cloud and Claude Code. The app included a media gallery, memory submission system with approval workflow, email notifications via Resend, a blog, event management, and a donor-facing section. She used ChatGPT to craft her initial prompt, then handed it to Claude Code along with a visual reference. The project went from localhost to a live URL on GitHub-connected Laravel Cloud with minimal friction. Kayla notes that while developers remain essential for scalable production apps, AI tooling now opens up a new world for internal tools and personal projects for non-technical builders.

recent_posts.title: Laravel April Product Updates
recent_posts.summary: Laravel's April updates bring several notable additions across the framework and its ecosystem. The core framework gains full-stack Passkeys support via laravel/passkeys with React, Vue, and Svelte helpers, debounceable queued jobs using a #[DebounceFor] attribute to collapse bursty dispatches, and MCP UI App Support for rendering sandboxed HTML apps inside MCP tools. Laravel Cloud adds a fully responsive mobile UI and dedicated edge network enhancements for monitoring and converting top IPs/paths into firewall or cache rules. Laravel Forge now supports PHP 8.5, multiple SSL certificates per site for staged rotations, and certificate renewal alerts to prevent downtime.

recent_posts.title: Laravel - The clean stack for Artisans and agents
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of building a production-ready SaaS application using the Laravel ecosystem. Covers bootstrapping with Laravel Starter Kits, improving AI-assisted development with Laravel Boost (MCP-based context for coding agents), adding social login via Socialite, handling Stripe billing with Cashier, implementing feature flags and plan-based access with Pennant, and deploying with Laravel Cloud. Uses a fictional app called TeamPulse as the running example throughout.

recent_posts.title: Laravel MCP Apps let tools return interactive HTML inside AI chat
recent_posts.summary: Laravel's MCP package now supports MCP Apps, allowing MCP tools to return interactive HTML interfaces rendered inline inside AI chat hosts like Claude, Claude Desktop, VS Code Copilot, and Goose. Instead of returning plain text, tools can serve sandboxed iframe UIs with full access to MCP server tools, bidirectional messaging with the model, and no separate auth layer. A single artisan command scaffolds a PHP resource class and Blade view. The package handles all protocol complexity automatically: capability advertisement, URI schemes, CSP headers, Tailwind dark mode configuration, and tool visibility controls. An open-source reference implementation called Locket ships two working MCP Apps as real-world examples.

recent_posts.title: Why hire a Laravel Partner agency for your next project
recent_posts.summary: Laravel's official Partner Program connects clients with vetted agencies that have deep expertise in the Laravel ecosystem. The program has two tiers — Community and Premier — with Premier Partners working directly with the Laravel team on larger or enterprise deployments. Partners are curated across geography, agency size, and industry specialization, and many contribute back to the ecosystem through open-source packages, meetups, and conferences. Hiring a Laravel Partner reduces project risk, accelerates ramp-up, and provides a direct line to the Laravel team when needed.

recent_posts.title: Laravel Cloud Pre-Check: Is Your App Ready to Deploy?
recent_posts.summary: Laravel has partnered with Jason McCreary and Laravel Shift to release a free static analysis tool called the Laravel Cloud Pre-Check. It connects to your GitHub, Bitbucket, or GitLab repository and generates a compatibility report delivered as a pull request in minutes. The report checks PHP version requirements, PHP extensions, Laravel Octane configuration, database configuration, system command calls, and hardcoded paths. Results fall into three categories: ready for Cloud, warnings, or blockers — each with actionable guidance so developers know exactly what to fix before migrating to Laravel Cloud.

recent_posts.title: Building an AI-powered CRM MVP with Laravel in under a week
recent_posts.summary: A senior freelance PHP developer shares how he built an AI-powered CRM MVP for an emergency response center in under a week using Laravel. The stack included Laravel Herd for local development, Laravel Cloud for CI/CD and deployment, Tailwind CSS and Alpine.js for the frontend, and the Laravel AI SDK with OpenAI Whisper for voice transcription. Push notifications via Laravel WebPush enabled a PWA experience indistinguishable from a native app. The project's success has the developer considering turning it into a multi-tenant micro-SaaS.

recent_posts.title: From Laravel Forge to Cloud: How Filament 3xed Performance
recent_posts.summary: Filament, one of the most popular open source Laravel packages with 23 million installs, migrated from Laravel Forge to Laravel Cloud and achieved 3x faster request speeds. The migration took just three hours and unlocked autoscaling, one-click Laravel Octane via FrankenPHP, Serverless Postgres, and managed Valkey caching. Day-to-day infrastructure shrank from an 8GB/8CPU server to 2GB replicas that scale up to 10 during traffic spikes and back down automatically. The serverless database also resolved a recurring issue where hourly demo data resets degraded live user experience. While Cloud costs are comparable or slightly higher, the capabilities gained — autoscaling, managed database, Octane, worker clusters — would have required managing at least 4x more servers on Forge.

recent_posts.title: How Filament migrated from Laravel Forge to Cloud and achieved 3x faster requests
recent_posts.summary: Filament, one of the most popular open source Laravel packages with 23 million installs, migrated from Laravel Forge to Laravel Cloud after hitting capacity limits during traffic spikes. The migration delivered a 3x improvement in request speed (2x from Cloud infrastructure, plus another boost from enabling Laravel Octane), autoscaling that handled 34 million network responses in two weeks without manual intervention, and 4x smaller replicas per instance. The entire migration of two applications took Dan Harrin just three hours. Key infrastructure changes included moving to Serverless Postgres, Laravel Valkey for caching, and separate worker clusters. While Cloud costs are comparable to the previous Forge setup, the capabilities — autoscaling, managed Octane, serverless database — represent a fundamentally different infrastructure tier.

recent_posts.title: Meet Maestro: How We Manage 21 Laravel Starter Kit Variants
recent_posts.summary: Maestro is an internal orchestration tool built by the Laravel team to manage 21 starter kit variants across 8 repositories. Instead of manually propagating changes across every repo, Maestro uses a layered build system where shared, framework-specific, auth-specific, and feature-specific layers are composed into final runnable kits. Contributors work on a built variant in a single directory, and a watcher syncs changes back to the correct source layer using priority-based ownership logic. Placeholder restoration ensures framework-specific values don't leak into shared source files. The tool also provides CLI commands for linting, validation, and browser testing across the full matrix or a targeted subset, significantly reducing the cognitive overhead for contributors.
